title: ActiveCampaign vs Mailchimp vs Brevo: B2B Prices and Contact Caps
desc: ActiveCampaign vs Mailchimp vs Brevo for B2B email: prices at four list sizes, who bills for unsubscribed contacts, Brevo's contact caps and which has a CRM.
question: Which is cheaper for B2B email, ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp or Brevo, and how does each count contacts?
keywords: activecampaign vs mailchimp, mailchimp vs activecampaign, brevo vs mailchimp, brevo vs activecampaign, activecampaign vs mailchimp vs brevo, brevo pricing, activecampaign pricing, mailchimp pricing, brevo alternatives, b2b email marketing software
cta: Running a B2B newsletter with sales in another CRM?
body:
Short answer. It depends on list size and on how you pay. On list prices read 18 November 2026, ActiveCampaign Starter (billed yearly) was the lowest at 1,000 contacts ($15 a month) and 2,500 ($39), and Brevo Standard (billed monthly) at 5,000 ($69) and 10,000 ($89). At 5,000 contacts Mailchimp Essentials was $75, ActiveCampaign Starter $79, Kit Creator $89 and Mailchimp Standard $100. Eligible new Mailchimp customers pay half for 12 months, which makes Essentials the lowest at every size we priced in that year ($13.25 to $55 a month). The bigger difference is what each tool counts: Mailchimp bills for unsubscribed contacts, ActiveCampaign counts every contact on accounts opened since 3 November 2025, and Brevo ties a stored-contact cap to each send tier for accounts opened since 1 October 2025.

We earn a commission if you buy Kit through our links. We earn nothing from ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp or Brevo. Every price below was read on the vendor's own pricing page on 18 November 2026.

Prices at four B2B list sizes

For each tool the table shows its cheapest paid plan with marketing automation, plus Mailchimp Standard; free plans and Brevo Starter (no marketing automation on its card) are left out. Mailchimp's figures are list prices after its 12-month offer. Brevo's column is the cheapest send tier that stores the list and covers four emails per contact a month. ActiveCampaign prints only yearly-billed prices, so its column is on a different billing basis.

ContactsMailchimp EssentialsMailchimp StandardBrevo StandardKit CreatorActiveCampaign Starter, billed yearly
1,000$26.50$45$35 (10,000 sends)$39$15
2,500$45$60$49 (15,000 sends)$59 (3,000 step)$39
5,000$75$100$69 (20,000 sends)$89$79
10,000$110$135$89 (40,000 sends)$139$149

How to read it:

  • Mailchimp: its pricing page currently offers 50% off for 12 months, then "starts at" the figures above, billed monthly. Its offer terms limit the discount to a "new Mailchimp customer or existing Free plan customer within 90 days of account creation in select countries" on a monthly plan. During the offer, Essentials is $13.25, $22.50, $37.50 and $55 a month at the four sizes, and Standard $22.50, $30, $50 and $67.50. At 1,000 contacts Essentials is the cheapest plan here billed monthly, but its automation flows are limited to 4 steps.
  • Brevo: its pricing page shows Standard from $18 a month for 5,000 sends, and 10% less on yearly billing. At 1,000 contacts you need the 10,000-send tier, because the 5,000 tier stores only 500 contacts.
  • Kit: its pricing page has price points at 1,000, 3,000, 5,000, 8,000 and 10,000 subscribers (and more above); the figures are billed monthly, and Kit says paying yearly saves 17%.
  • ActiveCampaign: its pricing page labelled every plan "Billed yearly" at the four sizes we read, and we found no monthly price on the page. Starter's $15 a month at 1,000 contacts is $180 billed for the year. Plus is $49, $95, $145 and $189 a month at the four sizes, and Pro is $79, $149, $205 and $375. The price selector goes from 2,500 contacts straight to 5,000, where Starter roughly doubles from $39 to $79.

How each tool counts your contacts

ToolCounts toward your contact limitExceptions
Mailchimp"Subscribed, unsubscribed, and non-subscribed contacts", across all audiencesArchived, cleaned and deleted contacts
ActiveCampaignAccounts opened on or after 3 November 2025: "All contacts, regardless of their list status"Older accounts: active or all contacts, depending on the plan
BrevoStored contacts, capped by send tier: 500, 1,500, 2,500, then 500,000 from 20,000 sendsAccounts opened before 1 October 2025 keep their old plan
KitSubscribers "only counted if they are unique and active"Kit's table does not define "active"

Sources: Mailchimp's pricing plans article, ActiveCampaign's contact limit article (updated 3 November 2026), Brevo's plans article and terms, and Kit's plan table. On Mailchimp, going over your tier brings "an additional charge on your bill" rather than a pause, as long as overages are paid on time. A hypothetical Mailchimp Standard account with 5,000 subscribed and 600 unsubscribed contacts holds 5,600 contacts, which falls in the 5,001 to 10,000 tier: $135 a month instead of $100, unless the 600 are archived. ActiveCampaign caps Starter at 25,000 contacts and suggests turning on its auto-upgrade, without which "your contact limit will not automatically increase".

Brevo's contact caps and the 2,501st contact

Brevo prices its paid plans by monthly sends. For accounts opened from 1 October 2025, its terms for the Standard plan say the number of contacts you may store "scales according to your selected monthly email volume". On Standard, 5,000 sends holds up to 500 contacts, 10,000 holds 1,500, 15,000 holds 2,500, and every tier from 20,000 sends holds up to 500,000.

That makes 2,500 contacts a price step. A 2,500-contact list fits the 15,000-send tier at $49 a month. The 2,501st contact needs the 20,000-send tier at $69: $20 a month more, or about 41%, even if you send the same number of emails. Brevo's terms say it "may automatically increase the Contacts limit in your account and upgrade your plan accordingly". Brevo's own quotas article lists the caps as "500, 1,500, or 500,000", leaving out the 2,500 tier its pricing article shows, so check the tier in your own account before you budget.

Brevo is not alone. Mailchimp's 2,501st contact moves Standard from $60 to $100 and Essentials from $45 to $75, about 67% more. ActiveCampaign's selector goes from 2,500 contacts ($39 for Starter) to 5,000 ($79), with no price shown in between, and Kit goes from $59 at 3,000 subscribers to $89 at 5,000.

Worked cost: 5,000 contacts and four emails a month

A hypothetical B2B team with 5,000 contacts sends a monthly newsletter plus a three-email nurture sequence: four emails per contact, 20,000 sends a month. List prices on 18 November 2026:

PlanPer monthA yearBilledSends allowed
Brevo Standard, 20,000 sends$69$828Monthly20,000
Mailchimp Essentials, 2,501 to 5,000$75$900Monthly50,000 (10 times contacts)
ActiveCampaign Starter, 5,000$79$948Yearly50,000
Kit Creator, 5,000$89$1,068MonthlyUnlimited broadcasts
Mailchimp Standard, 2,501 to 5,000$100$1,200Monthly60,000 (12 times contacts)
Kit Pro, 5,000$139$1,668MonthlyUnlimited broadcasts
ActiveCampaign Plus, 5,000$145$1,740Yearly50,000

Four things change the order.

  • Paying yearly: Brevo's 20,000-send tier drops to $62.08 a month ($744.96 a year) and Kit Creator to $890 a year, against $948 for ActiveCampaign Starter. Mailchimp's pricing page (17 November) lists annual plans for Premium and Standard at 10,000 or more contacts, through sales.
  • Mailchimp's offer: eligible new customers in select countries pay $37.50 for Essentials and $50 for Standard for the first 12 months ($450 and $600 for that year), less than any other plan in the table.
  • Sends: Brevo's price is set by sends, so the same team sending eight emails a month (40,000 sends) pays $89.
  • Seats: for three users, Mailchimp Essentials stays at $75 (3 seats included), Brevo Standard is $93 ($69 plus two extra seats at $12 each), Mailchimp Standard stays at $100 (5 seats), and Kit needs Pro at $139 billed monthly (or $1,043 for the first year on its current yearly offer), because Creator allows 2 users. ActiveCampaign includes 3 seats from Pro, at $205 a month billed yearly; its page prints no price for extra seats.

Mailchimp Essentials flows are limited to 4 steps, so check that your sequence fits.

Deals, pipelines and lead scoring for sales teams

If sales works deals in the same tool as email, the four differ more than their prices.

  • ActiveCampaign: its pricing table lists pipeline management, deal records, account records and lead scoring as "Included in add-on" (the Pipelines add-on) on Plus, Pro and Enterprise, and "Not included" on Starter. The add-on price is not printed, and Plus itself is $145 a month at 5,000 contacts, billed yearly. Its comparison page against Mailchimp, a vendor page (August 2026), says Starter "gives you access to a CRM", although the pricing table includes no deals or lead scoring on Starter.
  • Brevo: every plan includes "50 open deals and 1 sales pipeline". Sales Essentials adds unlimited deals and pipelines plus sales automation for $31 a month with 1 seat included.
  • Mailchimp: its plan comparison page lists a "Marketing CRM" feature, and the words pipeline, deal and lead scoring do not appear on it.
  • Kit: its pricing page does not mention a CRM or a pipeline. Pro lists "Subscriber engagement scoring", which, on our reading of the name, scores engagement rather than sales fit.

For how scoring models work and which tools score leads, see our guide to lead scoring software, and for tools that run sales follow-up rather than newsletters, our page on sales automation software.

ActiveCampaignStarter 1, Plus 1, Pro 3, Enterprise 5No free plan among its four plan cards; a "Free trial" link
KitFree 1, Creator 2, Pro unlimitedUp to 10,000 subscribers

Mailchimp's pricing page contradicts itself on the free plan: one line says "Under 250 contacts It's free", another says to try the Free plan "If your business has fewer than 500 contacts". Its help article says 250, and we use that figure.

Where Kit fits, and where it does not

Kit is our affiliate, so here is the case against it first. On list prices billed monthly, Kit Creator costs more than Mailchimp Essentials at every size in our table ($12.50 to $29 a month more at list price, and $25.75 to $84 more during Mailchimp's offer year for eligible customers), and more than Brevo Standard at every size ($4 more at 1,000, $20 more at 5,000, $50 more at 10,000). It costs more than ActiveCampaign Starter at 1,000, 2,500 and 5,000, although Starter's prices are billed yearly. Creator allows 2 users, and Kit's pricing page does not mention a deal pipeline or CRM, so a sales team would still need one elsewhere.

On yearly billing Kit does better: Creator is $890 a year at 5,000 subscribers against $948 for ActiveCampaign Starter, though $390 at 1,000 against $180. In our view, Kit fits a different B2B team: one that runs a newsletter or a content program and keeps sales in another CRM. Kit says it counts only "unique and active" subscribers, without defining active on its pricing page. If that is your setup, Kit's pricing page offers a 14-day free trial of Creator with no credit card required. We compared it with Mailchimp in more depth in Kit vs Mailchimp.

Which one we would pick for a B2B team

These are our suggestions, not the vendors' claims.

  • Email and a light sales pipeline in one tool, on a budget: we would start with Brevo Standard and its free pipeline, and watch the 2,500-contact step (Mailchimp and ActiveCampaign have one near the same size).
  • The cheapest first year, if you qualify: Mailchimp Essentials on its offer ($13.25 to $55 a month). Archive unsubscribed contacts, and price the second year at the full rate before you commit.
  • The lowest list price for a small list, paid yearly: ActiveCampaign Starter ($180 a year at 1,000 contacts, $468 at 2,500), if you can do without deals and lead scoring, which Starter does not include.
  • Lead scoring and deals tied to automations: ActiveCampaign Plus with the Pipelines add-on, once you have the add-on price in writing.
  • A newsletter-led program with sales in another CRM: Kit Creator, which costs more than Mailchimp Essentials and Brevo Standard at every size we priced.

Whichever you pick, we would keep newsletters and cold outreach on separate sending domains. Our email infrastructure service covers domains, inboxes, authentication and warm-up for outbound sending, and our AI automation agency page describes the workflow work we take on. For timings and channels in a nurture sequence, see lead nurturing email automation.

Not verified on 18 November 2026: ActiveCampaign's monthly-billing prices, its prices between the selector sizes and the price of its Pipelines add-on (none is printed on its pricing page); which countries qualify for Mailchimp's offer, and Mailchimp's annual-plan prices; whether Brevo counts unsubscribed contacts toward its caps. Prices change often, so check each vendor's page before you buy.
faqs: It depends on list size and on the year. On list prices billed monthly (18 November 2026), Brevo Standard is cheaper at 5,000 contacts ($69 for 20,000 sends, against $75 for Mailchimp Essentials and $100 for Standard) and at 10,000; Mailchimp Essentials is cheaper at 1,000 ($26.50 against $35) and at 2,500 ($45 against $49). During Mailchimp's 12-month offer for eligible new customers in select countries, Essentials and Standard both cost less than Brevo at every size we priced, for example $37.50 and $50 at 5,000 contacts.
Does Mailchimp charge for unsubscribed contacts?

Yes. Mailchimp's help says subscribed, unsubscribed and non-subscribed contacts are included in your contact count, and archived, cleaned and deleted contacts are not. Archiving unsubscribed contacts keeps them off the bill.

On its pricing page on 18 November 2026, ActiveCampaign Starter was $15 a month for 1,000 contacts, $39 for 2,500, $79 for 5,000 and $149 for 10,000, and Plus was $49, $95, $145 and $189, all billed yearly. The page printed no monthly-billing prices and no price for the Pipelines add-on that adds deals and lead scoring to Plus and above.
Does Brevo limit the number of contacts?

Yes. For accounts opened from 1 October 2025 (older accounts keep their current plan), on Starter and Standard, 5,000 sends a month holds up to 500 contacts, 10,000 holds 1,500, 15,000 holds 2,500 and 20,000 or more holds up to 500,000. The Free plan stores up to 100,000 contacts with 300 sends a day.
Which of ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp and Brevo has a CRM for B2B sales?

Brevo includes 50 open deals and 1 sales pipeline on every plan, and Sales Essentials adds unlimited deals and pipelines for $31 a month billed monthly. ActiveCampaign puts pipelines, deal records and lead scoring in a Pipelines add-on on Plus and above; the add-on price is not printed on its pricing page. Mailchimp's plan comparison lists a Marketing CRM feature but does not mention pipelines, deals or lead scoring.
Is Kit a good alternative to Mailchimp for B2B?

For a newsletter-led program it can be: Kit says it counts only unique and active subscribers, and its Free plan covers up to 10,000. On list prices billed monthly, Kit Creator costs $12.50 to $29 a month more than Mailchimp Essentials at the four sizes we priced; it is $11 less than Mailchimp Standard at 5,000 subscribers but $4 more at 10,000, and during Mailchimp's 12-month offer for eligible customers both Mailchimp plans cost less. Creator allows 2 users, and Kit's pricing page does not mention a CRM. We earn a commission on Kit.
